samples.summary: Header/footer caret renderer still uses the top-level-only table lookup the delta just replaced, so a caret the new code can now place inside a *nested* header/footer cell has no pixel to draw at
samples.evidence: `computeHFTableCellCaretPixel` resolves the cell with `hfLayout.blocks.find((b) => b.block.id === cellInfo.tableBlockId)` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:391) and returns `undefined` when that misses (line 394). An inner table is never a member of `hfLayout.blocks` — exactly the reason the delta swapped this pattern for `resolveNestedTableLayout` in `getVisualLineRange` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4071). `computeHFCursorPixel` (editor.ts:483-491) routes every non-top-level block here, so for a caret in a table nested inside a header/footer table the whole caret pixel is dropped, while Home/End/wrap-affinity in that same cell now resolve correctly. The body path (`resolvePositionPixel`, peer-cursor.ts:106-131) already walks the nesting chain; this is the one caret resolver that does not. Fix belongs here, not on the new code.

samples.summary: Up/Down visual-line navigation inside a cell still resolves the table with the non-nested `layout.blocks.find`, so it stays depth-1 while wrap affinity / Home / End are now depth-agnostic
samples.evidence: `const tl = this.getActiveLayout().blocks.find(b => b.block.id === tableBlockId)?.layoutTable;` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:2539, and the identical `tl2` at :2642) is the same lookup the delta removed from `getVisualLineRange`. For a block in a nested cell `tl` is `undefined`, so `moveCellLine` (:3147) is never called and Arrow Up/Down falls through to block-level navigation, jumping whole blocks instead of one visual line. After this delta the caret's `lineAffinity` can legitimately be 'forward' in a nested cell (consumed at :3173 inside `moveCellLine`), so the two paths now disagree about the same position. Pre-existing, but it is the sibling site of the fix and the inconsistency is newly reachable.

samples.summary: Fallback block length now comes from the (possibly stale) layout snapshot instead of the live document
samples.evidence: The fallback changed from `getBlockTextLength(this.doc.getBlock(pos.blockId))` to `getBlockTextLength(cell.blocks[cbi])`, where `cell` is derived from `resolved.dataBlock` — the block object held by the layout, which the new comment itself acknowledges may predate the local edit being described ('a layout computed before the local insertion'). The sole consumer that mixes the two, `getVisualLineEnd` (packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4123-4133), compares this `lineEnd` against `getBlockTextLength(this.doc.getBlock(pos.blockId))` from the *live* doc, so a stale snapshot can make End land short of the real line end right after a keystroke that has not been re-laid-out. Reading the live block for the length-only fallback would keep the old contract without reintroducing a throw.

finding.summary: Rewritten `getWrapAffinity` can now throw where it previously returned 'backward' (doc.getBlock on a stale layout)
finding.evidence: The old `getWrapAffinity` only did `layout.blocks.find(...)` and could not throw. It now delegates to `getVisualLineRange`, whose cell branch calls `this.doc.getBlock(cellInfo.tableBlockId)` (text-editor.ts:4062) and `this.doc.getBlock(pos.blockId)` (text-editor.ts:4085); `Doc.getBlock` throws `Block not found` (packages/docs/src/model/document.ts:187), and the branch also dereferences `tableBlock.tableData!.rows[...]` unchecked. `cellInfo` comes from the cached layout's `blockParentMap` (`getCellInfo`, text-editor.ts:3134-3139), so if the layout is momentarily stale relative to the model — e.g. `setCompositionStartPosition` (text-editor.ts:333) which is documented as running *after a remote change*, or the paste paths at text-editor.ts:3646/3701/3773 — an entry that names a table the model no longer has turns a formerly harmless 'backward' into an uncaught exception on the typing/IME/paste path. Fix belongs on the new `getWrapAffinity`/`getVisualLineRange` (use the non-throwing `doc.findBlock`, or guard). To confirm: whether any caller can reach `getWrapAffinity` while `blockParentMap` names a block absent from the model.

verdict.reason: The claimed throwing code is not present. In packages/docs/src/view/text-editor.ts:4050-4109, `getVisualLineRange`'s cell branch makes no `doc.getBlock` call at all: line 4062 is a comment and 4085 is `lineChars += run.charEnd - run.charStart`. The table is resolved entirely from the layout via `resolveNestedTableLayout(cellInfo.tableBlockId, layout)` (4071), with fully optional-chained lookups `resolved?.layoutTable.cells[...]?.[...]` (4072) and `resolved?.dataBlock.tableData?.rows[...]?.cells[...]` (4073-4074) — no `tableData!` deref. The guard at 4076 makes any stale/mismatched shape fall through to the non-throwing tail `layout.blocks.find(...)` / `if (!lb) return [0, 0]` (4101-4102), i.e. it degrades to 'backward' exactly as the old implementation did. `resolveNestedTableLayout` (table-layout.ts:338-431) is a pure layout function that takes no Doc and returns undefined on every mismatch (352, 371, 384, 409, 424). A grep of every `doc.getBlock` in text-editor.ts confirms none occurs between 4050 and 4109; the nearest is `getVisualLineEnd` at 4124, a separate method that `getWrapAffinity` (4150-4153, which calls only `getVisualLineRange`) never reaches. With no reachable throw, the caller-bypass premise (333, 3647, 3702, 3774) is moot.
